priceSnapshot.note: THE CEILING BROKE. Midnight named one number as the real limit of this leg - the daily EMA200 at 71,684.3 - and said it sat 1,901.7 points overhead. Price went through it four hours later. The 08:00Z hourly bar opened 69,829.5 and closed 71,588.4, a 1,758.9-point single-hour range, and the 10:00Z bar printed the session high at 72,495.0. The EMA200 recomputes to 71,704.0 on this run's 300-bar 1Dutc window and spot sits 188.5 points above it. Two other things resolved with it. Midnight's add gate at 70,064.2 required a settled hourly close above the highest print of the move; the 08:00Z bar settled 1,524.2 points above it, so the gate fired cleanly. And Farside's 19 August row, which had been showing IBIT and FBTC as dashes for two consecutive reports, filled in overnight at +284.7m and +62.4m for a day total of +517.2m - the largest single-day US spot-ETF inflow in the visible window and the direct explanation for the hour that broke the average. What did NOT break is the next shelf up. The session high of 72,495.0 stopped 13.0 points below the 29 May daily low at 72,508.0, the first structural memory above the June collapse. That is a measured rejection at real structure, not an arbitrary stall.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $71,704.0 - the daily EMA200 as computed this run. This is the level the whole thesis now rests on: it was the ceiling for eleven weeks, price is 188.5 points above it, and a reclaim that fails to hold on a closing basis is a bull trap rather than a breakout. Be honest about the geometry: 188.5 points is well inside the 1H ATR of 653.4, so an ordinary hourly bar can reach it without meaning anything. That is why the trigger is a settled CLOSE and not a touch. Below it the structure steps down to 71,417.4, the 2 June daily high, and then to 70,688.0, the 1 June daily low, which is where the reclaim genuinely fails.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $72,508.0 - the 29 May daily low, the first shelf of the pre-June range. The session high of 72,495.0 stopped 13.0 points short of it, which makes it a tested ceiling rather than a projected one. Above it the next measured levels are 72,584.1 (28 May low), 73,185.0 (30 May low) and 73,402.1 (31 May low), so a clean break opens roughly 900 points of thin tape. The qualifier is severe and it is why this is a gate rather than a plan: the 4H RSI is 89.0 and the 1H is 83.8, both the highest readings this file has recorded, and price sits 7.89 percent above the 4H ema20. Any break taken here is a momentum trade with a fast stop.

decisionBox.changed: Stance flips from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT, and the reason is positioning rather than price. Midnight's ADD rested on an explicit asymmetry: the long/short account ratio had fallen to 1.05, the least long-crowded reading in the visible window, open interest was rising, and the perpetual traded at a discount - new money was arriving SHORT into the highs, so there was fuel above and nothing to flush below. That asymmetry has inverted inside seven hours. The account ratio has climbed back from 1.05 to 1.13, and open interest has FALLEN 0.67 percent from 2,238,221,065 to 2,223,188,154 USD while price rose 3.02 percent. Open interest falling into a vertical move is the signature of short covering, not of new buying: 17,666,337 USD of short liquidations against 2,229,556 long in the last five and a half hours, a 7.92-to-1 skew, is the short book being removed rather than longs being added. The fuel that carried price through the EMA200 has largely been spent, and the accounts replacing it are long. So this trims 20 percent of the spot core at 71,892.5 into the first real structural resistance since the June collapse, keeps 80 percent exposed to a genuinely improved structure, and rebuilds the dry powder the last three sessions kept complaining about not having. The reduce line moves UP hard from 68,916.6 to 71,704.0 because the EMA200 is now the level that defines the thesis, and invalidation moves up from 68,385.6 to 70,688.0, the 1 June daily low. No resting stop: the gap to midday is five and a half hours of European and US cash-session liquidity, not an overnight void, and the US open at 09:30 ET is a scheduled event with MSTR and COIN already gapping - a stop parked inside that is a donation.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull reads BALANCED and that is a deliberate downgrade from midnight's UP. The realized tape is overwhelmingly one-sided - 17,666,337 USD of short liquidations against 2,229,556 long over five and a half hours, 7.92 to 1, and 9,441,501 against 2,156,653 in the last three hours alone. But realized data maps where the fuel WAS, and the three heaviest bands (72,250, 71,750 and 72,000) now bracket spot within 360 points in both directions rather than sitting above it. The forward reading comes from the positioning instead, and it has flipped: the long/short account ratio is back up to 1.13 from 1.05 at midnight, while open interest FELL 0.67 percent to 2,223,188,154 USD as price rose 3.02 percent. Fewer contracts and proportionally more long accounts after a vertical move means shorts closed out and longs stepped in at the highs - the exact inverse of the setup midnight bought. Funding still settles at the 0.0001 base rate with a premium of -0.000478, so the perpetual holds a small discount to spot and there is no funding stress yet; that is the one reading that has not turned. Honest caveat unchanged: this is REALIZED liquidation data, not a forward heatmap of resting orders. No CoinGlass key is configured, so the true forward map remains unavailable.

Shorter horizons from the same live series: 985.9 on the 4H, 653.4 on the 1H and 358.5 on the 15m. Every one of these has EXPANDED since midnight - the daily from 1,544.2, the 4H from 850.2, the 1H from 532.6 and the 15m from 223.5. Midnight read a decaying volatility spike and called it the signature of a shelf; the 08:00Z bar ended that. Volatility is re-expanding into the move, which is what a real breakout looks like and also what makes any stop measured in points buy less protection now than it did seven hours ago.

scalpContext.intradayBias: Digesting a vertical hour under a measured ceiling. The range that matters is 71,704.0 to 72,508.0 - the reclaimed daily EMA200 underneath and the 29 May daily low overhead - and spot sits in the lower third of it. Longs only work above 72,508.0 on a close, and even then the 4H RSI at 89.0 means fast management rather than a position. Shorts only work below 71,704.0 on a close, and the air pocket between 70,250 and 69,510 is where that trade would actually pay. In between is the worst possible place to take size. Volatility context matters this morning: the 1H ATR has expanded from 532.6 to 653.4 and the 15m from 223.5 to 358.5, so a stop measured in points buys materially less protection than it did at midnight. The US cash open at 09:30 ET is 2h20m after this report and MSTR is indicated +9.67 percent pre-market - that is the next real catalyst, not the chart.

etfFlows.note: THE UNKNOWN RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED BIG. The 19 August Farside row had been showing IBIT and FBTC as dashes through two consecutive reports - endday flagged it as the single largest scheduled unknown of the overnight gap and midnight reported it still unfilled. It filled overnight: IBIT +284.7m and FBTC +62.4m, taking the 19 August total to +517.2m. That is the largest single-day US spot-ETF inflow in the visible window, more than the 17 and 18 August days combined, and it is the direct explanation for the 08:00Z hourly bar that took price through the daily EMA200. Three consecutive positive days now read 17 August +297.5m, 18 August +189.3m and 19 August +517.2m, +1,004.0m across the streak. The 20 August row is all dashes as expected - US funds have not reported today and will not until this evening.

liquidations.note: skew is the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at the 11:00Z print, not a USD ratio. It has RISEN from 1.05 at midnight through 1.04, 1.14, 1.09, 1.12 to 1.13 now - long accounts are rebuilding at the highs, reversing the read that justified midnight's ADD. The more important number sits next to it: open interest FELL 0.67 percent from 2,238,221,065 to 2,223,188,154 USD while price rose 3.02 percent. Contracts leaving the market during a vertical rally means the move was driven by shorts closing, not by longs opening, and the realized tape agrees - 17,666,337 USD of short liquidations against 2,229,556 long across 1,600 fills between 06:35Z and 11:57Z, 7.92 to 1. Funding still settles at the base 0.0001 with a premium of -0.000478, so the perpetual holds a small discount to spot and there is no long-side funding stress yet. The synthesis: the structure improved and the fuel that improved it is largely spent.

calibration.note: The prior report is 2026-08-20-midnight, published at 02:20:00-05:00 with spot at 69,782.6. It grades YES on both counts and this one is not close. Its reduce line at 68,916.6 was never approached - the lowest print since publication is the 69,510.0 low of the 07:00Z hourly bar, 593.4 points clear - so priorReduceFired is false. Its add gate at 70,064.2 required a settled hourly close above the highest print of the whole move, and the 08:00Z bar settled 71,588.4, clearing it by 1,524.2 points; add_fired is true. Acting on it helped twice over: the 15.00 USDT of spot it deployed at 69,782.6 is worth 71,892.5 now, plus 3.02 percent, and it correctly switched OFF the resting stop endday had recommended at 68,850.0 - a stop there would have survived anyway, but the reasoning was right for the right reason. The sharper credit belongs to the mechanism rather than the direction. Midnight did not predict a breakout; it identified the exact number that would define one (the daily EMA200), stated the positioning condition that made the upside asymmetric (account ratio at 1.05, open interest rising, perpetual at a discount, no long crowding to flush), and deployed a partial tranche against it while naming the three reasons to hold the rest back. Two of those three reasons have now resolved - the Farside row filled at +517.2m and the gate fired - and the third, the 4H RSI, has got worse rather than better at 89.0. That is why this session trims instead of adding: the same discipline that justified buying a 1.05 account ratio has to justify selling a 1.13 one with open interest falling.
